articles.title: Crypto bosses, CEOs and F1: Singapore's business events boom gathers pace

paras.en: Billionaires, global CEOs and crypto executives descended on Singapore last week as a growing number of high-profile conferences coincided with the country's Formula 1 Grand Prix.
paras.zh: 上周，随着越来越多的高调会议与新加坡一级方程式大奖赛同时举行，亿万富翁、全球首席执行官和加密货币高管齐聚新加坡。

paras.en: More than 40 business events were held around this year's Grand Prix period, up from over 25 in 2025 and over 30 in 2024, according to the Singapore Tourism Board. The events included the Milken Institute Asia Summit, TOKEN2049, the Forbes Global CEO Conference, Solana Summit APAC and the Global-Asia Family Office Summit.
paras.zh: 据新加坡旅游局称，今年大奖赛期间举办了 40 多场商业活动，高于 2025 年的 25 场和 2024 年的 30 多场。这些活动包括米尔肯研究所亚洲峰会、TOKEN2049、福布斯全球首席执行官会议、Solana 亚太区峰会以及全球-亚洲家族办公室峰会。

paras.en: Formula 1 has generated more than 2.2 billion Singapore dollars ($1.72 billion) in incremental tourism receipts between its debut in 2008 and 2024, according to Singapore's Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry, which equates to an average of S$150 million each. The race itself costs approximately S$140 million a year to organize, METI said, though noted it isn't directly comparable with the revenue generated.
paras.zh: 据新加坡能源、贸易和工业部称，从 2008 年首次举办到 2024 年，一级方程式赛车已创造了超过 22 亿新元（17.2 亿美元）的增量旅游收入，相当于平均每项 1.5 亿新元。 METI 表示，赛事本身每年的组织成本约为 1.4 亿新元，但指出这与产生的收入无法直接比较。

paras.en: Singapore GP said the 2026 race drew 301,294 spectators, the second-highest attendance in the event's history.
paras.zh: 新加坡大奖赛表示，2026 年比赛吸引了 301,294 名观众，这是该赛事历史上第二高的观众人数。

paras.en: Business events themselves are becoming a larger source of tourism revenue. Receipts from meetings, incentives, conventions and exhibitions (MICE) rose 35% to S$2.3 billion in 2025, outpacing the 10% growth in Singapore's overall tourism receipts to a record S$32.8 billion, data from STB showed.
paras.zh: 商业活动本身正在成为旅游收入的更大来源。新加坡旅游局的数据显示，2025 年会议、奖励旅游、会议和展览 (MICE) 收入增长 35%，达到 23 亿新元，超过新加坡整体旅游收入 10% 的增幅，达到创纪录的 328 亿新元。

paras.en: Singapore's Tourism Board noted that MICE visitors typically spend significantly more than leisure travelers.
paras.zh: 新加坡旅游局指出，会展游客的消费通常比休闲游客高得多。

paras.en: Organizers are increasingly capitalizing on the excitement surrounding Formula 1 to extend delegates' stays, according to Poh Chi Chuan, executive director of exhibitions and conferences at STB.
paras.zh: STB 展览和会议执行董事 Poh Chi Chuan 表示，组织者越来越多地利用一级方程式赛车带来的兴奋来延长代表们的停留时间。

paras.en: "This creates a natural gravitational pull, when the city is buzzing and the right target audience is already flying in, savvy planners build on that momentum," Poh said.
paras.zh: “这会产生一种自然的引力，当城市热闹起来并且合适的目标受众已经涌入时，精明的规划者就会利用这种势头，”Poh 说。

paras.en: At TOKEN2049, one of the world's major cryptocurrency conferences, overseas attendees accounted for 85.6% of participants this year, up from 82.7% in 2025, according to figures provided by the event organizer. The figures classify overseas attendees as those who are not Singaporean nationals.
paras.zh: 根据活动主办方提供的数据，在全球主要加密货币会议之一的 TOKEN2049 上，今年海外参会者占参会者的 85.6%，高于 2025 年的 82.7%。这些数字将海外与会者归类为非新加坡国民。

paras.en: Chinese attendees accounted for 11.8% of participants, nearly double the 6% share recorded last year, overtaking Americans as the largest group.
paras.zh: 中国参与者占参与者的 11.8%，几乎是去年 6% 的两倍，超过美国人成为最大群体。

paras.en: The influx of business travelers also coincided with strong demand at Singapore's luxury hotels.
paras.zh: 商务旅客的涌入也恰逢新加坡豪华酒店的强劲需求。

paras.en: Marina Bay Sands said its hotel, the iconic three-towered building often featured in photos of the Singapore skyline, operated at near-full occupancy during the Formula 1 period.
paras.zh: 滨海湾金沙表示，其酒店是新加坡天际线照片中经常出现的标志性三塔建筑，在一级方程式赛车期间几乎客满。

paras.en: The integrated resort also hosted TOKEN2049 at its Expo & Convention Centre, underscoring how major business conferences and sporting events are increasingly overlapping.
paras.zh: 该综合度假村还在其会展中心举办了 TOKEN2049，凸显了大型商务会议和体育赛事日益重叠。

paras.en: For the hotel industry overall, the clustering of MICE events and Formula 1 helped propel rates to record levels last year.
paras.zh: 对于整个酒店业来说，MICE 活动和一级方程式赛车的聚集帮助推动去年的房价达到创纪录的水平。

paras.en: In October 2025, average room rates rose 19.5% from a year earlier to S$384.15, according to hospitality data provider CoStar. On the opening day of that race weekend, hotel occupancy reached 95.9% and the average room rate jumped to S$757.62.
paras.zh: 根据酒店数据提供商 CoStar 的数据，2025 年 10 月，平均房价同比上涨 19.5% 至 384.15 新元。比赛周末开幕当天，酒店入住率达到 95.9%，平均房价跃升至 757.62 新元。

articles.title: Stock futures are little changed as traders await consumer inflation report: Live updates

paras.en: U.S. stock futures were up early Wednesday as the release of September's consumer inflation report loomed.
paras.zh: 由于九月份消费者通胀报告即将发布，美国股指期货周三早盘上涨。

paras.en: S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.22% and 0.29%, respectively, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures edged 0.14% higher.
paras.zh: 标准普尔 500 指数期货和纳斯达克 100 指数期货分别上涨 0.22% 和 0.29%，道琼斯工业平均指数期货小幅上涨 0.14%。

paras.en: Bank of America shares declined over 2% in extended trading after the firm was hit with more than $1.2 billion in federal penalties, with regulators saying the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in "suspicious" transactions.
paras.zh: 美国银行 (Bank of America) 受到超过 12 亿美元的联邦处罚，监管机构称该银行未能报告超过 50 亿美元的“可疑”交易，该公司股价在盘后交易中下跌超过 2%。

paras.en: In Asia, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.62%. Japan's Nikkei 225 added 0.32%, while South Korea's Kospi rose 0.82%.
paras.zh: 在亚洲，澳大利亚 S&P/ASX 200 指数下跌 0.62%。日本日经225指数上涨0.32%，韩国综合指数上涨0.82%。

paras.en: A drift downward in chip stocks weighed on the major averages Tuesday, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) falling for a sixth straight session over growing fears of an AI spending bubble and rising anxieties around competition out of China.
paras.zh: 周二，芯片股的下跌打压了主要股指，VanEck 半导体 ETF (SMH) 连续第六个交易日下跌，原因是人们对人工智能支出泡沫的担忧日益加剧，以及对中国竞争的担忧加剧。

paras.en: A swath of big banks posted strong quarterly results, but shares ended the day lower, with Goldman Sachs and Citigroup falling. The market's reaction suggested businesses have a higher bar to clear during the third-quarter earnings season — especially in tech where semiconductors are expected to be the largest contributor to year-over-year earnings growth.
paras.zh: 多家大型银行公布了强劲的季度业绩，但股价当天收低，其中高盛和花旗集团下跌。市场的反应表明，企业在第三季度财报季节需要克服更高的门槛，尤其是在科技行业，半导体预计将成为同比盈利增长的最大贡献者。

paras.en: S&P 500 companies are expected to post a blended earnings growth rate of roughly 30%, while semiconductors and semiconductor equipment are set for growth of 130%, according to FactSet data.
paras.zh: FactSet 数据显示，标准普尔 500 指数公司的综合盈利增长率预计将达到 30% 左右，而半导体和半导体设备的增长率将达到 130%。

paras.en: "The business fundamentals are very strong. It's very hard to argue with the demand side of the story for chips," Marta Norton, chief investment strategist at Empower, told CNBC's "Closing Bell: Overtime." "I don't know if we necessarily question how good those business fundamentals are as much as we question how much valuation is left in the space."
paras.zh: Empower 首席投资策略师玛塔·诺顿 (Marta Norton) 在 CNBC 节目《收盘钟声：加班》中表示：“业务基本面非常强劲。芯片需求方面的情况很难反驳。” “我不知道我们是否一定会质疑这些业务基本面有多好，就像我们质疑该领域的估值还剩多少一样。”

paras.en: Investors are awaiting the September reading of the U.S. consumer price index Wednesday morning. Economists polled by Dow Jones anticipate inflation to have risen by 3.6% on a year-over-year basis, up from 3.4% in the prior reading.
paras.zh: 投资者正在等待周三上午公布的美国 9 月份消费者价格指数。道琼斯调查的经济学家预计通胀率将同比上升 3.6%，高于上次数据中的 3.4%。

paras.en: The results arrive as oil prices remain elevated and consumers pay more for gasoline, which is averaging at $4.34 a gallon, compared to $3.08 per gallon a year earlier, according to AAA. Last week President Donald Trump announced he would temporarily ease restrictions on Russian diesel fuel exports, but analysts don't believe the deal will do much to lower fuel prices for truckers and farmers.
paras.zh: 根据 AAA 的数据，这一结果的出现是由于油价持续走高，消费者为汽油支付了更高的价格，平均价格为每加仑 4.34 美元，而一年前为每加仑 3.08 美元。上周，唐纳德·特朗普总统宣布他将暂时放松对俄罗斯柴油出口的限制，但分析人士认为，该协议不会对降低卡车司机和农民的燃油价格产生太大作用。

paras.en: Earnings season continues, with more big bank results from Bank of America and Morgan Stanley out Wednesday morning U.S. time. Dutch semiconductor company ASML also reports.
paras.zh: 美国时间周三上午，美国银行和摩根士丹利将公布更多大型银行业绩，财报季仍在继续。荷兰半导体公司 ASML 也有报道。

articles.title: Judge extends block on Trump White House ban of MS NOW, CNN and Politico

paras.en: A federal judge late Tuesday night indefinitely extended his block on the White House from enforcing a ban on three media outlets that President Donald Trump announced in mid-September.
paras.zh: 周二深夜，一名联邦法官无限期延长了白宫对唐纳德·特朗普总统于九月中旬宣布的对三家媒体的禁令的禁令。

paras.en: The preliminary injunction by Judge Timothy Kelly replaces his temporary restraining order against Trump's ban of MS NOW, CNN and Politico from the White House complex as a lawsuit challenging the ban plays out.
paras.zh: 蒂莫西·凯利法官的初步禁令取代了针对特朗普禁止 MS NOW、CNN 和 Politico 进入白宫大楼的临时限制令，因为针对该禁令的诉讼正在进行中。

paras.en: "President Trump's own comments suggest that he intended the revocation of Plaintiffs' hard passes to alter their reporting on him," wrote Kelly, who was nominated by Trump for his seat in U.S. District Court in Washington.
paras.zh: 凯利写道：“特朗普总统本人的言论表明，他打算撤销原告的硬通行证，以改变他们对他的报道。”凯利被特朗普提名担任华盛顿美国地方法院的席位。

paras.en: In his written opinion, Kelly said the three outlets were likely to succeed on their claim in their pending lawsuit, which argues they were denied due process when Trump summarily barred them without giving them a chance to argue against it.
paras.zh: 凯利在书面意见中表示，这三个媒体很可能在未决诉讼中胜诉，该诉讼称，当特朗普立即禁止他们，而不给他们机会反对时，他们被拒绝了正当程序。

paras.en: The judge cited two existing opinions by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, which establish a due process right to journalists whose White House passes are targeted for revocation. Those appellate opinions are binding on federal District Court judges in D.C.
paras.zh: 法官引用了美国哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院的两项现有意见，其中规定了白宫通行证被撤销的记者的正当程序权利。这些上诉意见对华盛顿特区联邦地方法院法官具有约束力。

paras.en: The judge also said, for the first time in this case, the outlets were likely to succeed on two First Amendment claims in their civil suit, which allege retaliation and viewpoint discrimination.
paras.zh: 法官还表示，在本案中，媒体首次有可能在民事诉讼中的两项第一修正案诉讼中取得成功，这两项诉讼指控报复和观点歧视。

paras.en: Kelly's order Tuesday is not a final ruling on the merits of the suit. And it does not compel the White House to restore access to the Oval Office and Air Force One to the outlets.
paras.zh: 凯利周二的命令并不是对该诉讼案情的最终裁决。而且它并不迫使白宫恢复椭圆形办公室和空军一号的出口通道。

paras.en: Kelly brushed aside the Department of Justice's claim that in addition to concerns about inaccurate news stories, Trump decided to revoke the outlets' access to the White House on national security grounds.
paras.zh: 凯利驳斥了司法部的说法，即除了对不准确新闻报道的担忧之外，特朗普还决定以国家安全为由取消这些媒体进入白宫的权限。

paras.en: "There is no evidence in the record that President Trump made the decision to revoke Plaintiffs' hard passes on national security grounds from the get-go, nor at any time has he directly stated that national security was the reason for his decision," Kelly wrote.
paras.zh: 凯利写道：“记录中没有证据表明特朗普总统从一开始就以国家安全为由决定撤销原告的强硬通过，他也没有在任何时候直接表示国家安全是他做出这一决定的原因。”

paras.en: The judge said the DOJ's national security argument appears to be "merely a post-hoc justification for the decision" after the outlets sued.
paras.zh: 法官表示，在媒体提起诉讼后，司法部的国家安全论点似乎“只是该决定的事后理由”。

paras.en: "Still, no one should interpret the Court's decision to suggest that President Trump's concerns about accuracy and fairness in the media's reporting are unfounded, or that the government is powerless when its true aim is to protect national security when classified information is unlawfully disclosed," Kelly wrote.
paras.zh: 凯利写道：“尽管如此，任何人都不应将法院的裁决解读为特朗普总统对媒体报道的准确性和公平性的担忧是毫无根据的，或者当政府的真正目的是在机密信息被非法披露时保护国家安全时，政府却无能为力。”

paras.en: "That said, for the reasons explained below, the Court will extend the relief it already ordered, which will continue to preserve the status quo while this case proceeds," Kelly said, referring to his prior order that restored access by the outlets to the White House.
paras.zh: 凯利说：“尽管如此，出于下文解释的原因，法院将延长已经下令的救济，在本案继续审理期间，这将继续维持现状。”他指的是他之前恢复媒体进入白宫的命令。

paras.en: The judge said that without the preliminary injunction, the outlets were "likely to suffer irreparable harm."
paras.zh: 法官表示，如果没有初步禁令，这些媒体“可能会遭受无法弥补的伤害”。

paras.en: His ruling came on the heels of a court hearing last Thursday, when the DOJ defended the ban, which reportedly led to 78 journalists having their so-called hard passes to the White House revoked before Kelly ordered them restored with his previous temporary restraining order.
paras.zh: 他的裁决是在上周四的法庭听证会上做出的，当时司法部为这项禁令进行了辩护，据报道，该禁令导致 78 名记者的所谓“硬通行证”被撤销，随后凯利用之前的临时限制令下令恢复这些记者的通行证。

paras.en: Trump last month said he would appeal any decision by Kelly blocking his ban. CNBC has requested comment from the White House and DOJ.
paras.zh: 特朗普上个月表示，他将对凯利阻止其禁令的任何决定提出上诉。 CNBC 已要求白宫和司法部发表评论。

paras.en: Theodore Boutrous Jr., an attorney for the outlets, said in a statement, "We are grateful that the Court ruled in favor of our clients."
paras.zh: 这些媒体的律师西奥多·布特鲁斯 (​​Theodore Boutrous Jr.) 在一份声明中表示：“我们很高兴法院做出了有利于我们客户的裁决。”

paras.en: "When the President issued his 'ban on the free press,' he blatantly and explicitly violated due process and the First Amendment," Boutrous said. "Since then, the President has repeatedly, candidly, and consistently admitted in public that he banned our clients from the White House to punish reporting he doesn't like and to try to force journalists to cover him in ways he prefers."
paras.zh: “当总统发布‘新闻自由禁令’时，他公然、明确地违反了正当程序和第一修正案，”布特鲁斯说。 “从那时起，总统一再、坦诚、持续地公开承认，他禁止我们的客户进入白宫，是为了惩罚他不喜欢的报道，并试图迫使记者以他喜欢的方式报道他。”

paras.en: "The harm this ban did to our clients, the First Amendment, and the public as a whole is profound," the attorney said. "The Court was right to enjoin the White House from enforcing this "unconstitutional ban on the free press" for the foreseeable future."
paras.zh: “这项禁令对我们的客户、第一修正案以及整个公众造成的伤害是深远的，”律师说。 “法院禁止白宫在可预见的未来执行这项“违反宪法的新闻自由禁令”是正确的。”

paras.en: Trump on Sept. 18 said that he was banning the three outlets because of how they have covered him.
paras.zh: 特朗普于 9 月 18 日表示，他将禁止这三个媒体，因为它们对他的报道方式。

paras.en: In a Truth Social post that day, Trump wrote that the outlets "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America."
paras.zh: 特朗普在当天的《真相社会》帖子中写道，媒体“在报道美国总统、特朗普政府或美利坚合众国时，不应该不断地撰写或报道虚构和谎言。”

paras.en: Trump later said that same day that he had become "sick" of "cumulative stories" by the outlets.
paras.zh: 特朗普当天后来表示，他已经“厌倦”了媒体的“累积故事”。

paras.en: The ban took effect on the following day, Sept. 19, when journalists from the outlets were denied access to the White House grounds and had their permanent passes confiscated by Secret Service officers.
paras.zh: 该禁令于第二天（9 月 19 日）生效，当时各媒体的记者被拒绝进入白宫，特勤局官员还没收了他们的永久通行证。

paras.en: The outlets sued Trump on Sept. 21 in a civil complaint that said, "This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles."
paras.zh: 这些媒体于 9 月 21 日在一份民事诉状中起诉特朗普，称“这项禁令是对第一修正案的直接攻击，也是对我们最基本宪法原则的公然违反。”

paras.en: Kelly, two days later, issued a restraining order that temporarily reversed the ban for at least 14 days. Journalists from the three outlets on Sept. 24 were allowed to return to the White House, and since then Kelly extended the restraining order to allow him time to consider whether to issue Tuesday's preliminary injunction, which has no set expiration date.
paras.zh: 两天后，凯利发布了一项限制令，暂时撤销了至少 14 天的禁令。 9月24日，这三个媒体的记者被允许返回白宫，此后凯利延长了限制令，以便让他有时间考虑是否发布周二的初步禁令，该禁令没有设定到期日期。

articles.title: Scientists worry AI is stealing their ideas

paras.en: Recently, controversy and accusations have followed artificial intelligence companies flexing their models’ research capabilities. When OpenAI claimed an internal model had solved one of math’s seven million-dollar problems, a mathematician at New York University insinuated that the company had stolen his progress, which he had shared with one of their chatbots. Weeks later, the New York Times reported a similar story unfolding between Anthropic and a biologist at the University of Copenhagen regarding a group of enzymes.
paras.zh: 最近，随着人工智能公司展示其模型的研究能力，引发了争议和指控。当 OpenAI 声称内部模型已经解决了价值 700 万美元的数学问题之一时，纽约大学的一位数学家暗示该公司窃取了他的进展，并将其与他们的一个聊天机器人分享。几周后，《纽约时报》报道了人类和哥本哈根大学生物学家之间关于一组酶的类似故事。

paras.en: Despite this, scientists from all disciplines are opting to use these companies’ large language models. Some use them as a soundboard or a tool for literature review, others for cleaning up nearly finished work. And mathematicians and theorists are tapping their new, powerful models to generate entire proofs for their research. But as researchers feed more of their data and ideas into these models, concerns are growing about how that content is getting used.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，各个学科的科学家都选择使用这些公司的大型语言模型。有些人用它们作为音板或文献综述的工具，另一些人则用它们来清理即将完成的工作。数学家和理论家正在利用他们新的、强大的模型来为他们的研究生成完整的证明。但随着研究人员将更多的数据和想法输入到这些模型中，人们越来越担心这些内容的使用方式。

paras.en: Both OpenAI and Anthropic stated unequivocally that they did not train their models on the mathematician’s and biologist’s uploaded data, respectively. But the companies—which have not consistently met academic norms—don’t have every scientist’s trust. Some suspect they may not even have the full picture themselves. Their agents could be accessing data in ways the companies don’t even realize. After all, it took three months for the public to learn that OpenAI’s models had breached containment and hacked into foreign government databases.
paras.zh: OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都明确表示，他们没有分别根据数学家和生物学家上传的数据来训练模型。但这些公司并没有始终如一地符合学术规范，并没有得到所有科学家的信任。有些人怀疑他们自己可能还没有全面了解。他们的代理人可能会以公司甚至没有意识到的方式访问数据。毕竟，公众花了三个月的时间才得知 OpenAI 的模型突破了遏制并侵入了外国政府数据库。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: With these conspiracy theories swirling, some researchers are now seeing the models more as competitors than tools—and the use of them as a betrayal. “I’m not encouraging it, and I’m not doing it myself,” says Clément Canonne, a theoretical computer scientist at the University of Sydney. “I’m not using them.”
paras.zh: 随着这些阴谋论的蔓延，一些研究人员现在将这些模型更多地视为竞争对手而不是工具，并将它们的使用视为背叛。 “我并不鼓励这样做，我自己也不会这样做，”悉尼大学理论计算机科学家克莱门特·卡农 (Clément Canonne) 说。 “我没有使用它们。”

paras.en: Ahead of taking their companies public, OpenAI and Anthropic are increasingly stepping into math and science to show how capable their products are. But AI has sometimes felt less like a guest over for dinner and more like an unwanted visitor breaking and entering. If scientists feel that these companies are rifling through their every interaction, they may start locking them out entirely.
paras.zh: 在公司上市之前，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 越来越多地涉足数学和科学领域，以展示他们的产品的能力。但人工智能有时感觉不像是来吃晚饭的客人，而更像是闯入的不速之客。如果科学家认为这些公司正在仔细检查他们的每一次互动，他们可能会开始将他们完全拒之门外。

paras.en: The lack of transparency invites these sorts of fears. “Right now, these systems infer things about you without telling you that they’re inferring things about you,” says Jennifer King, a fellow at the Stanford University Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, who researches data privacy and policy.
paras.zh: 缺乏透明度会引发此类担忧。斯坦福大学以人为中心的人工智能研究所研究数据隐私和政策的研究员詹妮弗·金 (Jennifer King) 表示：“目前，这些系统在推断有关你的事情时，却没有告诉你它们正在推断有关你的事情。”

paras.en: King says the only way for researchers to really ensure their safety when using large language models at the present moment is to look at their account settings carefully. According to her, “enterprise” accounts—which represent a special deal worked out between a client company and the AI’s owners—seem to be safe. “But if you are on a personal account, all bets are off,” she warns. She describes how users on personal accounts need to explicitly opt out in many cases to prevent their information being used from training.
paras.zh: King 表示，目前研究人员在使用大型语言模型时真正确保安全的唯一方法是仔细查看他们的帐户设置。据她说，“企业”账户——代表客户公司和人工智能所有者之间达成的特殊交易——似乎是安全的。 “但如果你使用的是个人账户，那么所有的赌注都将落空，”她警告说。她描述了个人帐户用户在许多情况下如何需要明确选择退出，以防止他们的信息被用于培训。

paras.en: Plus, even if a company isn’t intentionally using your data to train their models, one of their many agents could always go rogue, infiltrating company data and hoovering up individual users’ conversations with their chatbots. While there is no evidence this happened in the case of any of the AI companies’ scientific discoveries, rogue events over the summer have left some extra concerned about who they trust with their data.
paras.zh: 另外，即使一家公司没有故意使用你的数据来训练他们的模型，他们的众多代理之一也可能总是会变得流氓，渗透公司数据并收集个人用户与其聊天机器人的对话。虽然没有证据表明人工智能公司的任何科学发现都发生过这种情况，但今年夏天发生的流氓事件让一些人更加担心他们信任谁来处理他们的数据。

paras.en: The trouble is, it’s hard to get much evidence at all out of the tech giants. “The companies are not transparent about these practices, so it’s really hard to pin down,” King says. That means experts can’t speculate about any particular case. But in general, “the companies spy on you and use that information against you,” says Bruce Schneier, a security researcher and activist.
paras.zh: 问题是，很难从科技巨头那里获得太多证据。 “这些公司对这些做法并不透明，因此很难确定，”金说。这意味着专家无法推测任何特定案例。但总的来说，“这些公司会监视你，并利用这些信息来对付你，”安全研究员兼活动家布鲁斯·施奈尔 (Bruce Schneier) 说。

paras.en: The new AI models are very capable, including for research, and many believe they will help researchers find new results faster. So scientists may feel they face a choice: either use the models and risk leaking a discovery or don’t and risk someone who does publishing it first.
paras.zh: 新的人工智能模型非常强大，包括在研究方面，许多人相信它们将帮助研究人员更快地找到新结果。因此，科学家们可能觉得他们面临着一个选择：要么使用模型并冒着泄露发现的风险，要么不使用模型并冒着让先发表该模型的人面临风险的风险。

paras.en: All this has created an uneasy landscape in which many scientists are left feeling they have to give up their privacy and work to keep up. “There is definitely a pressure,” Canonne says. “If you’re not using them, are you going to be irrelevant?”
paras.zh: 所有这一切造成了一种令人不安的局面，许多科学家感到他们必须放弃自己的隐私并努力跟上。 “压力肯定是存在的，”卡农说。 “如果你不使用它们，你就会变得无关紧要吗？”

articles.title: Latest Trump administration proposal to change NIH research grant system draws scientists’ ire

paras.en: The National Institutes of Health is weighing changes to the procedures it uses to allot scientific funding. Experts say the change—concealing scores on applications for grants—could reduce transparency around how federal money is spent on research.
paras.zh: 美国国立卫生研究院正在考虑改变其科学经费分配程序。专家表示，这一改变——隐藏拨款申请分数——可能会降低联邦资金用于研究的透明度。

paras.en: Currently, applications for NIH grants are examined by at least three experts in the applicant’s field of research. That panel of peer reviewers then submits a written review that summarizes the likely outcomes of the proposed research, as well as the application’s strengths and weakness. The reviewers also each give the application a score between 1 and 9, with 1 being the highest. An average of these, called the impact score, is revealed to the applicant.
paras.zh: 目前，美国国立卫生研究院资助的申请由申请人研究领域的至少三名专家进行审查。然后，同行评审小组提交一份书面评审，总结拟议研究的可能结果，以及应用程序的优点和缺点。评审员还分别给该应用程序打分 1 到 9 分，其中 1 分最高。这些平均值（称为影响分数）会向申请人透露。

paras.en: Under the proposed changes, grant applicants wouldn’t find out their impact score. Instead they would be told whether their application landed in one of three broad buckets: the top 25 percent, or “most competitive,” the next 25 percent, or “competitive,” and the bottom 50 percent, or “not discussed.” The latter category would mean an application did not even warrant extended discussion among the peer reviewers.
paras.zh: 根据拟议的变更，资助申请人将无法得知他们的影响分数。相反，他们会被告知他们的应用程序是否属于三大类别之一：前 25%，或“最具竞争力”，接下来的 25%，或“有竞争力”，以及最后 50%，或“未讨论”。后一类意味着申请甚至不需要同行评审员之间进行广泛的讨论。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The proposal is designed to communicate “valuable information about the assessed scientific merit” and give program officers more flexibility on making awards, according to an NIH document outlining the rule change.
paras.zh: 根据美国国立卫生研究院概述规则变更的文件，该提案旨在传达“有关评估的科学价值的宝贵信息”，并为项目官员提供更灵活的奖励。

paras.en: “Discussed applications would still receive a resume of discussion and all applications would still receive written critiques from the assigned reviewers, to include individual criterion/factor scores,” the document states. But some scientists and research organizations have criticized the change as potentially reducing transparency and accountability.
paras.zh: 文件指出：“讨论过的申请仍将收到讨论简历，所有申请仍将收到指定审阅者的书面批评，包括个人标准/因素分数。”但一些科学家和研究组织批评这一变化可能会降低透明度和问责制。

paras.en: Joshua Weitz, a biology professor at the University of Maryland, said in a Substack post that the proposal could have disastrous results for the scientific community and lead to less transparency for both applicants and the NIH program officers charged with managing grant portfolios. Under the new system, he argued, an application that scored in the top 1 percent may be treated the same as one that scored lower but still within the top 25 percent.
paras.zh: 马里兰大学生物学教授 Joshua Weitz 在 Substack 帖子中表示，该提案可能会给科学界带来灾难性的结果，并导致申请人和负责管理拨款组合的 NIH 项目官员的透明度降低。他认为，在新系统下，得分位于前 1% 的应用程序可能会与得分较低但仍在前 25% 之内的应用程序受到相同的对待。

paras.en: “By concealing scores, the NIH proposal would make it harder for program officers to assess consensus, lead to greater uncertainty for applicants and undermine scientific peer review," Weitz tells Scientific American.
paras.zh: 韦茨告诉《科学美国人》：“通过隐藏分数，美国国立卫生研究院的提案将使项目官员更难评估共识，给申请人带来更大的不确定性，并破坏科学同行评审。”

paras.en: The proposal marks the latest way the Trump administration has tried to flex its muscles over scientific grants. Floated earlier this year, a separate bid to have political appointees, rather than peer review panels, decide grant recipients garnered significant backlash—and was put on hold until at least December after Congress rejected the change. “The NIH proposal should be interpreted in this broader context,” Weitz says.
paras.zh: 该提案标志着特朗普政府试图在科学资助方面展示实力的最新方式。今年早些时候，一项由政治任命者而不是同行评审小组来决定拨款接受者的单独提议遭到了强烈反对，并且在国会拒绝这一改变后至少被搁置到 12 月。 “美国国立卫生研究院的提案应该在更广泛的背景下进行解释，”韦茨说。

paras.en: “By reducing transparency and concealing quantitative feedback from experts serving on scientific review groups, the NIH proposal makes it harder for applicants and the public to understand the basis for grant award recommendations,” he adds. “In the absence of transparent data sharing, there is an increased risk that political priorities override scientific review in grant decisions.”
paras.zh: “通过降低透明度并隐藏科学审查小组专家的定量反馈，美国国立卫生研究院的提案使申请人和公众更难理解拨款建议的基础，”他补充道。 “如果缺乏透明的数据共享，拨款决策中政治优先事项凌驾于科学审查之上的风险就会增加。”

paras.en: The proposal’s public comment period opened in August and ends today. Other comments on the proposal from research groups echo Weitz’s caution.
paras.zh: 该提案的公众评议期于八月开始，今天结束。研究小组对该提案的其他评论也呼应了韦茨的谨慎态度。

paras.en: In a statement, the North American Vascular Biology Organization, which submitted a comment to the NIH, wrote that the proposed grant review system might “become significantly less transparent” and “will compromise accountability, and breed uncertainty, inefficiency, and distrust. It is also likely that the dearth of data regarding grant reviews will compromise the ability of Congress to exercise oversight and the agency’s own ability to assess and improve its funding choices.”
paras.zh: 向美国国立卫生研究院提交评论的北美血管生物学组织在一份声明中写道，拟议的拨款审查制度可能“变得更加不透明”，并且“将损害问责制，并滋生不确定性、低效率和不信任。有关拨款审查的数据缺乏也可能会损害国会行使监督的能力以及该机构自身评估和改进其资助选择的能力。”

paras.en: Meanwhile, Global Health Technologies Coalition (GHTC) wrote in a submitted comment that while it supports the NIH’s stated goal of ensuring funding decisions reflect the peer review process, any changes must “provide researchers with sufficient information to understand the scientific strengths and weaknesses” identified during peer review.
paras.zh: 与此同时，全球卫生技术联盟（GHTC）在提交的评论中写道，虽然它支持 NIH 确保资助决策反映同行评审过程的既定目标，但任何改变都必须“为研究人员提供足够的信息，以了解同行评审期间发现的科学优势和劣势”。

paras.en: “Researchers and institutions have experienced significant changes to NIH funding policies, priorities, and grantmaking practices over the past year,” GHTC wrote. “Additional reforms should be implemented in a measured and thoughtful manner and clearly communicated to stakeholders to minimize unnecessary disruption to the research ecosystem.”
paras.zh: GHTC 写道：“过去一年，研究人员和机构经历了 NIH 资助政策、优先事项和资助实践的重大变化。” “额外的改革应该以谨慎和深思熟虑的方式实施，并明确地传达给利益相关者，以尽量减少对研究生态系统的不必要的破坏。”

paras.en: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the NIH, did not immediately return a request for comment.
paras.zh: 负责监督国家卫生研究院的美国卫生与公众服务部没有立即回复置评请求。

articles.title: Hurricane Isaias shows ‘it only takes one’ to wreak havoc after historically calm Atlantic hurricane season

paras.en: Hurricane Isaias may have arrived late in the Atlantic hurricane season, but the torrential rains and 105-mile-per-hour winds the storm brought to the U.S. Gulf Coast over the weekend were a sharp reminder of these weather events’ power to cause chaos.
paras.zh: 飓风伊萨亚斯可能在大西洋飓风季节较晚的时候到来，但周末给美国墨西哥湾沿岸带来的倾盆大雨和时速 105 英里的大风强烈提醒人们，这些天气事件有可能造成混乱。

paras.en: Hurricane Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane on Saturday, spawning tornadoes, destroying buildings and downing power lines across the Gulf region. As of Tuesday, the storm has killed at least four people, while thousands have remained without power.
paras.zh: 周六，伊萨亚斯飓风以 2 级飓风身份登陆，引发龙卷风，摧毁了整个海湾地区的建筑物并压垮了电线。截至周二，风暴已造成至少四人死亡，数千人仍处于断电状态。

paras.en: This destruction is typical for a hurricane—these are massive storms with surface winds that reach at least 74 mph. But Hurricane Isaias was far from normal: it was the first hurricane of an eerily quiet season and, by far, the latest first hurricane in an Atlantic season on record. But even the quietest hurricane seasons can bring chaos, says meteorologist Alan Gerard.
paras.zh: 这种破坏是飓风的典型特征——表面风速至少达到 74 英里/小时的大规模风暴。但伊萨亚斯飓风远非正常：这是一个异常安静的季节中的第一场飓风，也是迄今为止有记录的大西洋季节中最新的第一场飓风。但气象学家艾伦·杰拉德表示，即使是最安静的飓风季节也可能带来混乱。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “When I worked for [the National Weather Service], the agency started using the phrase ‘it only takes one’ to remind people that, even during a quiet hurricane season, a single storm can have tremendous impacts,” Gerard says. The situation with “2026 and Isaias is a perfect example of that.”
paras.zh: “当我在[国家气象局]工作时，该机构开始使用‘只需要一次’这句话来提醒人们，即使在平静的飓风季节，一场风暴也可能产生巨大的影响，”杰拉德说。 “2026 和伊萨亚斯的情况就是一个完美的例子。”

paras.en: This year’s “Super El Niño” has made it difficult for hurricanes to form in the Atlantic because of high wind shear causing rapidly changing high-speed winds in the upper atmosphere that effectively break storms apart. The Pacific, meanwhile, has seen historically high numbers of hurricanes because of low wind shear and warm ocean water—conditions also created by the El Niño.
paras.zh: 今年的“超级厄尔尼诺”现象使大西洋很难形成飓风，因为高风切变导致高层大气中的高速风迅速变化，有效地分解了风暴。与此同时，由于低风切变和温暖的海水（厄尔尼诺现象也造成了这些条件），太平洋地区的飓风数量创历史新高。

paras.en: Hurricane Isaias developed after that wind shear briefly died down off the Gulf Coast. With the help of extremely warm water in the Atlantic this fall, Isaias grew fast: it was upgraded from Category 1 to Category 3 overnight before it made landfall as a Category 2 storm. The storm took advantage of rare favorable conditions off the Gulf Coast, says Brian McNoldy, a hurricane researcher at the University of Miami.
paras.zh: 飓风伊萨亚斯是在墨西哥湾沿岸的风切变短暂减弱后发展起来的。今年秋天，在大西洋极温暖海水的帮助下，伊萨亚斯迅速成长：一夜之间从 1 级升级为 3 级，然后登陆为 2 级风暴。迈阿密大学飓风研​​究员布莱恩·麦克诺迪说，这场风暴利用了墨西哥湾沿岸罕见的有利条件。

paras.en: “It found one of the few spots in the Atlantic where a hurricane could have formed,” McNoldy says. “There was a pretty small window of opportunity.”
paras.zh: 麦克诺迪说：“它发现了大西洋上为数不多的可能形成飓风的地点之一。” “机会之窗非常小。”

paras.en: If we see another hurricane this season, he says, it, too, will likely land somewhere on the Gulf Coast. The Caribbean, which often sees late-season hurricanes throughout October, has especially high wind shear from the El Niño, so storms are not expected there.
paras.zh: 他说，如果我们这个季节看到另一场飓风，它也可能会登陆墨西哥湾沿岸的某个地方。加勒比地区在整个十月份经常出现晚季飓风，厄尔尼诺现象带来的风切变特别高，因此预计那里不会出现风暴。

paras.en: Though Isaias’s impact is relatively on par with a Category 2 hurricane, McNoldy says, “no hurricane is a small ordeal.” Even the quietest storm seasons can bring catastrophic destruction if the conditions are right, he says.
paras.zh: 尽管伊萨亚斯的影响与 2 级飓风相当，但麦克诺迪说，“没有一场飓风是小考验。”他说，如果条件合适，即使是最平静的风暴季节也可能带来灾难性的破坏。

paras.en: “No matter what the season is doing,” McNoldy adds, “you always have to be paying attention because you don’t know when a storm has your name on it.”
paras.zh: “无论这个季节发生什么，”麦克诺迪补充道，“你必须始终保持警惕，因为你不知道风暴什么时候会出现在你的名字上。”

articles.title: How the Grand Canyon could have lost 1 billion years of geologic history
articles.author: Lucas Van Wyk Joel

paras.en: In the Grand Canyon, rock layers preserve a relatively continuous record of Earth’s geologic history going back about 2 billion years. But between 520 million and 1.8 billion years, the record is noticeably empty. It’s as if someone broke into a museum and made off with almost an entire wing’s worth of rocks, and sorting out “whodunnit” is one of the coldest cases in all geology.
paras.zh: 在大峡谷中，岩层保存着相对连续的地球地质历史记录，可以追溯到大约 20 亿年前。但在 5.2 亿年到 18 亿年之间，记录明显是空的。这就好像有人闯入博物馆并偷走了几乎整个展馆的岩石，而整理“侦探小说”是所有地质学中最冷的案例之一。

paras.en: Now, scientists studying the Grand Canyon’s rocks say that a gigantic Earth-spanning cliff —with a global glaciation as its accomplice — could be to blame for the heist.
paras.zh: 现在，研究大峡谷岩石的科学家表示，一个横跨地球的巨大悬崖——全球冰川作用是其同谋——可能是这次盗窃事件的罪魁祸首。

paras.en: The giant cliff started forming about 800 million years ago as an ancient supercontinent called Rodinia split apart, Thomas Gernon, an earth scientist at the University of Southampton in England, and colleagues report August 17 in Geology. Forces like rain and ice weathered and eroded the rock and, like waves at the beach steadily erasing one layer of sand after another, deleted a billion years of Earth’s history.
paras.zh: 英国南安普顿大学地球科学家 Thomas Gernon 及其同事于 8 月 17 日在《地质学》杂志上报道称，大约 8 亿年前，当一块名为罗迪尼亚 (Rodinia) 的古老超级大陆分裂时，巨大的悬崖开始形成。雨水和冰等力量风化并侵蚀了岩石，就像海滩上的海浪不断地抹去一层又一层的沙子一样，抹去了地球十亿年的历史。

paras.en: The group used computer models to simulate how ancient Earth evolved over hundreds of millions of years. They watched as the cliff — known as an escarpment — formed around the time in Earth’s history when rocks in the region vanished.
paras.zh: 该小组使用计算机模型来模拟古代地球数亿年的演化过程。他们目睹了悬崖——被称为悬崖——是在地球历史上该地区岩石消失的那段时间形成的。

paras.en: The escarpment most likely extended across much of a continent called Laurentia, the ancient precursor to North America. It stretched from what was to become Alaska all the way to Arizona and would have been about one to two kilometers high.
paras.zh: 悬崖很可能横跨劳伦西亚大陆的大部分地区，劳伦西亚大陆是北美的古代前身。它从后来的阿拉斯加一直延伸到亚利桑那州，高约一到两公里。

paras.en: Some 65 million years ago, the Great Escarpment of Laurentia would have stretched across much of North America, including the spot that would one day become the Grand Canyon and the site of an enduring geologic mystery. The escarpment itself is thought to have formed around 800 million years ago.
paras.zh: 大约 6500 万年前，劳伦西亚大悬崖横跨北美大部分地区，其中包括有一天成为大峡谷的地方和一个持久的地质谜团所在。据认为，悬崖本身形成于大约 8 亿年前。

paras.en: “No study has previously suggested the existence of a continental-scale escarpment in the Grand Canyon region. Our study shows it’s a plausible, straightforward explanation for the immense erosion that took place in the Grand Canyon,” Gernon says. Such an immense cliff created steep slopes that were ideal places for the elements to loosen and make off with exposed rock.
paras.zh: “之前没有研究表明大峡谷地区存在大陆级悬崖。我们的研究表明，这是对大峡谷发生的巨大侵蚀的一个合理而直接的解释，”格农说。如此巨大的悬崖形成了陡峭的斜坡，是自然元素松动并剥落裸露岩石的理想场所。

paras.en: And the escarpment had a lot of help when it came to its disappearing act: ice, lots and lots of ice. The theft of the rocks coincided with an extreme period of glaciation called Snowball Earth. Massive ice sheets formed and may have extended all the way from the poles to equatorial latitudes. As the ice expanded, it would have eroded great quantities of rock, helping create the gap in the record.
paras.zh: 悬崖在消失过程中得到了很多帮助：冰，很多很多的冰。岩石失窃恰逢被称为“雪球地球”的极端冰川时期。巨大的冰盖形成，并可能从两极一直延伸到赤道纬度。随着冰层的扩张，它会侵蚀大量的岩石，从而造成了记录上的差距。

paras.en: And the escarpment, due to its high elevation, would have created ideal conditions for Snowball Earth glaciers and ice sheets to form. In a separate study published in Science, Gernon and a team explained how an escarpment created by tectonic activity was responsible for the formation of the East Antarctic Ice Sheet starting some 34 million years ago. “The exposed rocky peaks of the escarpment would have acted as glacier factories,” Gernon says.
paras.zh: 由于悬崖海拔较高，为雪球地球冰川和冰盖的形成创造了理想的条件。在《科学》杂志上发表的另一项研究中，Gernon 和他的团队解释了约 3400 万年前由构造活动形成的悬崖如何导致东南极冰盖的形成。 “悬崖上裸露的岩石山峰可以充当冰川工厂，”格农说。

paras.en: It remains unclear, however, whether the erosion that erased the rocks occurred before, during or after the Snowball Earth glaciations. “That’s the real hole that needs filling: pinning down the erosion history in space and time, continent by continent, precisely enough,” Gernon says.
paras.zh: 然而，目前尚不清楚消除岩石的侵蚀是否发生在雪球地球冰川作用之前、期间或之后。格农说：“这才是真正需要填补的漏洞：准确地确定各个大陆在空间和时间上的侵蚀历史。”

paras.en: Linking the disappearance of the rocks to verified events in Earth’s history such as the breakup of Rodinia bolsters the case, says Alan Collins, a geologist at Adelaide University in Australia who was not involved in the new study. Not only that, but Gernon’s team points to modern-day examples where similar erosive processes are at work, including a similar escarpment in Antarctica as well as one in South Africa.
paras.zh: 未参与这项新研究的澳大利亚阿德莱德大学地质学家艾伦·柯林斯 (Alan Collins) 表示，将岩石的消失与地球历史上已证实的事件（例如罗迪尼亚的分裂）联系起来，支持了这一论点。不仅如此，格农的团队还指出了类似侵蚀过程正在发挥作用的现代例子，包括南极洲和南非的类似悬崖。

paras.en: Maybe not quite case closed yet, but “I find this very convincing,” Collins says.
paras.zh: 也许案件尚未完全结束，但“我发现这非常有说服力，”柯林斯说。

articles.title: When climate change brings the heat, what happens to a mighty redwood?
articles.author: Allie Skalnik

paras.en: Towering coast redwoods are known for their resiliency, withstanding fire, fungus and rot to survive for centuries. But these ancient trees now may be vulnerable to a relatively recent foe: heat waves.
paras.zh: 高耸的海岸红杉以其生命力而闻名，能够抵御火灾、真菌和腐烂，能够存活几个世纪。但这些古老的树木现在可能容易受到最近的敌人的影响：热浪。

paras.en: As temperatures climb, photosynthesis slows in these iconic trees, researchers report September 22 in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences. Lab experiments show the rate of the sunlight-driven food making process in its needles roughly halves when temperatures rise from 30° to 40° Celsius.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 22 日在《地球物理研究杂志：生物地球科学》上报告称，随着气温上升，这些标志性树木的光合作用减慢。实验室实验表明，当温度从 30 摄氏度升至 40 摄氏度时，阳光驱动的针中食物制造过程的速度大约减半。

paras.en: Such a change usually indicates “severe levels of stress,” says Lily Klinek, an ecophysiologist at the University of California, Davis. That vulnerability can cause tree deaths that may jeopardize one of California’s largest stores of carbon, a shield against climate change.
paras.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的生态生理学家 Lily Klinek 表示，这种变化通常表明“压力很大”。这种脆弱性可能会导致树木死亡，从而可能危及加州最大的碳储存库之一，而碳储存库是应对气候变化的屏障。

paras.en: Coast redwoods (Sequoia sempervirens) live only in a narrow strip of coastal habitat from central California to southern Oregon, where temperatures are mild and fog is abundant. But recent heat waves have spiked temperatures in parts of their range to over 40° C.
paras.zh: 海岸红杉（Sequoia sempervirens）仅生活在从加利福尼亚州中部到俄勒冈州南部的狭长沿海栖息地，那里气温温和，雾气充足。但最近的热浪使部分地区的气温飙升至 40°C 以上。

paras.en: The impact of heat waves on photosynthesis has been studied in other tree species, with some faring better than others. But this is the first study to investigate how coast redwoods respond to the heat, says Troy Magney, an ecophysiologist at the University of Montana in Missoula.
paras.zh: 人们已经在其他树种中研究了热浪对光合作用的影响，其中一些树种的情况比其他树种更好。但这是第一项调查海岸红杉如何应对高温的研究，米苏拉蒙大拿大学的生态生理学家特洛伊·马格尼说。

paras.en: From July 2022 to October 2024, Klinek, Magney and colleagues repeatedly measured the performance of needles from redwoods in California’s Mendocino County. That period included two heat waves.
paras.zh: 从 2022 年 7 月到 2024 年 10 月，Klinek、Magney 和同事反复测量了加利福尼亚州门多西诺县红杉针的性能。那段时期经历了两次热浪。

paras.en: Typically, trees stay cool when small porelike openings called stomata allow water to evaporate, taking heat with it, similar to how sweat cools humans. But when conditions get too hot and dry, stomata close, retaining a plant’s moisture. Under extreme heat, the team found that needles reached up to 10 degrees C hotter than the surrounding air due to the dark needles absorbing ample sunlight. That suggests that the stomata were at least partially closed.
paras.zh: 通常情况下，当被称为气孔的小孔状开口允许水蒸发并带走热量时，树木就会保持凉爽，类似于人体出汗的方式。但当环境变得太热和干燥时，气孔就会关闭，保留植物的水分。在极端高温下，研究小组发现，由于黑色的针状物吸收了充足的阳光，针状物的温度比周围空气的温度高出10摄氏度。这表明气孔至少部分关闭。

paras.en: Those same pores are crucial for photosynthesis; it’s where the trees take in carbon dioxide — used to make food — and release oxygen. “They could essentially starve if they don’t have access to enough carbon,” Klinek says.
paras.zh: 这些毛孔对于光合作用至关重要。这是树木吸收二氧化碳（用于制造食物）并释放氧气的地方。 “如果它们无法获得足够的碳，它们基本上可能会挨饿，”克利内克说。

paras.en: It’s hard to investigate the impact of heat on photosynthesis in the field, though. That would take building a “heat chamber around a real-life branch or wait[ing] for a heat event to happen,” Klinek says. Instead, she climbed onto the roof of her car with a pole pruner and collected samples from about five meters high, in the lower canopy.
paras.zh: 不过，在野外研究热量对光合作用的影响是很困难的。克利内克说，这需要在现实生活中的树枝周围建造一个热室或等待热事件发生。相反，她拿着一把杆式修枝剪爬到车顶，在下部天篷约五米高处采集了样本。

paras.en: In the lab, the researchers subjected the samples to increasing heat to match the heat waves seen in recent summers and measured the resulting photosynthesis rates. Even though the samples were submerged in water, so had their stomata open and had full access to the ingredients for photosynthesis, the rate still declined. “They weren’t slowing their photosynthesis because of carbon starvation,” Klinek says.
paras.zh: 在实验室中，研究人员将样品置于不断增加的热量中，以匹配最近夏天出现的热浪，并测量了由此产生的光合作用速率。尽管样本浸没在水中，气孔打开并且可以充分获取光合作用的成分，但速率仍然下降。 “它们并没有因为碳匮乏而减慢光合作用，”克利内克说。

paras.en: For practical reasons, the study focused on younger coast redwoods, not the old growth giants. It’s difficult to reach even the lowest branches on trees more than 100 meters tall. “There are just fundamental limitations on what you can sample if you don’t have a jetpack,” says Christopher Still, an ecophysiologist at Oregon State University in Corvallis who was not associated with the study. Even so, the team’s results show that coast redwoods are “really temperature sensitive. You don’t see this as much with other species necessarily,” Still says.
paras.zh: 出于实际原因，该研究重点关注年轻的海岸红杉，而不是老树。 100多米高的树上，即使是最低的树枝也很困难。俄勒冈州立大学科瓦利斯分校的生态生理学家克里斯托弗·斯蒂尔（Christopher Still）并未参与这项研究，他表示：“如果没有喷气背包，你所能采集的样本就会受到根本性的限制。”即便如此，研究小组的结果表明，海岸红杉“确实对温度敏感。你在其他物种中不一定会看到这种情况，”斯蒂尔说。

paras.en: In the field, Klinek observed trees closing their stomata to preserve water. This suggests that in more realistic conditions, where a heat wave and drought hit simultaneously, lack of heat and water could make the slowdown “even more intense.” But more work needs to be done, she notes. “We still don’t know what the threshold is for irreversible damage.”
paras.zh: 在野外，克利内克观察到树木关闭气孔以保存水分。这表明，在更现实的条件下，即热浪和干旱同时袭来，缺乏热量和水可能会使经济放缓“更加严重”。但她指出，还需要做更多的工作。 “我们仍然不知道不可逆转损害的阈值是多少。”

articles.title: Scarred blood vessels may be one clue to APOE4’s Alzheimer’s risk
articles.author: RJ Mackenzie

paras.en: The gene APOE4 is the strongest common genetic risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease. But it’s still something of a mystery to researchers.
paras.zh: APOE4 基因是阿尔茨海默病最常见的遗传风险因素。但这对研究人员来说仍然是一个谜。

paras.en: Now, new work suggests one way the gene variant does its dirty work. It influences the production of scar tissue throughout vital vascular connections carrying blood to and from the brain, researchers report September 24 in Cell. This process may also contribute to the buildup of the protein amyloid-beta, which is thought to be one of the first signs of Alzheimer’s disease in the brain.
paras.zh: 现在，新的研究提出了基因变体进行肮脏工作的一种方式。研究人员于 9 月 24 日在《细胞》杂志上报道，它会影响将血液输送到大脑和从大脑输送血液的重要血管连接中疤痕组织的产生。这一过程也可能有助于β淀粉样蛋白的形成，这被认为是大脑中阿尔茨海默病的最初迹象之一。

paras.en: APOE4 is an allele, one of three slightly different, common forms of the APOE gene, which makes a protein that helps carry fats in the bloodstream. The variant is common among people who have Alzheimer’s disease. “If you had a room of 10 people with Alzheimer’s disease, and you asked how many of those people have the APOE4 allele, six of them would,” says neuroscientist Joel Blanchard of the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York City. Yet many people who carry APOE4 never develop the dementia-causing disease, leaving researchers trying to understand what the gene variant actually does to make the brain more vulnerable.
paras.zh: APOE4 是一种等位基因，是 APOE 基因的三种略有不同的常见形式之一，它产生一种有助于在血液中携带脂肪的蛋白质。这种变异在阿尔茨海默病患者中很常见。纽约市西奈山伊坎医学院的神经科学家乔尔·布兰查德 (Joel Blanchard) 表示：“如果房间里有 10 名患有阿尔茨海默氏症的人，你问其中有多少人携带 APOE4 等位基因，答案是其中有 6 人会携带。”然而，许多携带 APOE4 的人从未患上导致痴呆的疾病，这使得研究人员试图了解该基因变异实际上是如何使大脑更脆弱的。

paras.en: One clue came from people who seemed unusually resilient to that risk. In 2024, researchers examined more than 3,500 people, including some who carried two copies of APOE4 but had not developed Alzheimer’s. Genetic analysis showed that they had a mutation in their DNA that meant their blood vessels had far lower levels of a protein called fibronectin, a kind of cellular superglue that assists wound healing. The reserachers suggested that too much fibronectin could make it harder for the brain to clear amyloid-beta from the brain. A buildup of those plaques is a hallmark of the disease.
paras.zh: 一条线索来自那些似乎对这种风险异常有抵抗力的人。 2024 年，研究人员对 3,500 多人进行了检查，其中一些人携带两个 APOE4 拷贝，但并未患上阿尔茨海默病。基因分析显示，他们的 DNA 发生了突变，这意味着他们的血管中一种名为纤连蛋白的蛋白质含量要低得多，纤连蛋白是一种有助于伤口愈合的细胞强力胶。研究人员认为，过多的纤连蛋白可能会使大脑更难清除大脑中的β淀粉样蛋白。这些斑块的堆积是该疾病的标志。

paras.en: That result pushed Blanchard and his colleagues to look more closely at blood vessels. “The prevailing thought in the field is basically that the Alzheimer’s disease is so bad that the blood vessels break down,” Blanchard says. ”But we wanted to ask the question: Is it the other way around?”
paras.zh: 这一结果促使布兰查德和他的同事更加仔细地研究血管。布兰查德说：“该领域普遍认为，阿尔茨海默病非常严重，以至于血管会破裂。” “但我们想问一个问题：情况是否相反？”

paras.en: Blanchard and his colleagues built an atlas that mapped gene expression — how DNA is read and converted into proteins — across the human brain vasculature at a cellular level. Stitching together data from three existing brainwide maps, their atlas represented 66,000 cells from 220 people. They team examined how this map differed in people with two copies of APOE4 compared with those with less harmful gene variants.
paras.zh: 布兰查德和他的同事建立了一个图谱，在细胞水平上绘制了人类大脑脉管系统的基因表达——DNA如何被读取并转化为蛋白质。他们的图谱将来自三张现有全脑图谱的数据拼接在一起，代表了 220 人的 66,000 个细胞。他们的团队研究了这张图谱在携带两个 APOE4 拷贝的人与那些危害较小的基因变异的人之间有何不同。

paras.en: APOE4 carriers had fewer pericytes, starfish-shaped cells that wrap around and stabilize blood vessels. They also had higher numbers of myofibroblasts, cells normally formed during tissue injury that pump out fibronectin, the team found.
paras.zh: APOE4 携带者的周细胞较少，周细胞是包裹并稳定血管的海星状细胞。研究小组发现，它们的肌成纤维细胞数量也较多，这些细胞通常在组织损伤期间形成，可产生纤连蛋白。

paras.en: The map offered a snapshot, but it couldn’t show whether the missing pericytes were actually transforming into myofibroblasts. The researchers turned to 3-D models of human brain tissue grown from stem cells. In models carrying two copies of APOE4, pericytes began taking on the characteristics of scar-producing myofibroblasts. The transformation also offered a possible explanation for the earlier clue from resilient APOE4 carriers: Myofibroblasts produce large amounts of fibronectin. And when the researchers prevented cells in their models from producing fibronectin, amyloid accumulation dropped.
paras.zh: 该图提供了一个快照，但它无法显示缺失的周细胞是否实际上正在转化为肌成纤维细胞。研究人员转向利用干细胞生长的人脑组织的 3D 模型。在携带两个 APOE4 拷贝的模型中，周细胞开始呈现出产生疤痕的肌成纤维细胞的特征。这一转变还为弹性 APOE4 携带者的早期线索提供了可能的解释：肌成纤维细胞产生大量纤连蛋白。当研究人员阻止模型中的细胞产生纤连蛋白时，淀粉样蛋白的积累就会减少。

paras.en: The researchers also found a possible trigger for the cellular switch. In the APOE4 models, signaling through the immune molecule TGF-beta helped drive pericytes toward the scar-producing state. Blocking that signaling in cell models and aged mice restored the proportion of blood vessels wrapped up by pericytes.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现了细胞开关的可能触发因素。在 APOE4 模型中，通过免疫分子 TGF-β 发出的信号有助于驱动周细胞进入疤痕生成状态。在细胞模型和老年小鼠中阻断该信号传导可以恢复被周细胞包裹的血管比例。

paras.en: The TGF-beta data are “particularly interesting,” because inhibiting the protein reversed some of APOE4’s effects on pericytes, says Abdel Ali Belaidi, a neuroscientist at the Florey Institute of Neuroscience and Mental Health in Parkville, Australia. But TGF-beta performs many jobs throughout the body, he says, making it a difficult molecule to target safely with a drug.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚帕克维尔弗洛里神经科学与心理健康研究所的神经科学家 Abdel Ali Belaidi 表示，TGF-β 数据“特别有趣”，因为抑制该蛋白可以逆转 APOE4 对周细胞的一些影响。但他说，TGF-β 在全身发挥着多种作用，这使得它成为一种难以用药物安全靶向的分子。

paras.en: And damage to the brain’s blood vessels is only one of the many ways APOE4 has been linked to Alzheimer’s. Other studies have shown that the gene variant alters inflammation and interacts with another Alzheimer’s-linked protein, tau. How all these changes lock together to link APOE4 so strongly to Alzheimer’s disease is a greater mystery than one study can solve. ”As a field, we’re all progressing toward an answer,” Blanchard says.
paras.zh: 对大脑血管的损害只是 APOE4 与阿尔茨海默病相关的众多方式之一。其他研究表明，该基因变异会改变炎症并与另一种阿尔茨海默病相关蛋白 tau 相互作用。所有这些变化如何结合在一起，使 APOE4 与阿尔茨海默病如此紧密地联系在一起，这是一项研究无法解决的更大谜团。 “作为一个领域，我们都在寻找答案，”布兰查德说。

articles.title: Incredibly Creepy Video Shows You a Bee Stinger Like You've Never Seen It Before
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: The sharp stab of a bee sting hurts bad enough, but it's the venom that makes the pain last.
paras.zh: 蜜蜂的尖锐刺伤已经够痛的了，但毒液才让疼痛持续下去。

paras.en: The stingers of honeybees (Apis mellifera) are typically single-use. In the process of stabbing their target's skin, the bee's stinger is ripped from its rear, leaving a considerable wound that the bee later dies from.
paras.zh: 蜜蜂（Apis mellifera）的毒刺通常是一次性的。在刺伤目标皮肤的过程中，蜜蜂的毒刺从后方被撕开，留下相当大的伤口，蜜蜂随后死亡。

paras.en: But even after the doomed bee has flown away, the stinger keeps on pumping.
paras.zh: 但即使在注定失败的蜜蜂飞走之后，毒刺仍继续抽动。

paras.en: As part of a new study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, scientists have captured a disembodied stinger in action to better understand how they work.
paras.zh: 作为发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上的一项新研究的一部分，科学家们捕捉到了一只正在活动的无实体毒刺，以更好地了解它们的工作原理。

paras.en: It's a little disturbing, but also we can't look away. See for yourself in the video below.
paras.zh: 这有点令人不安，但我们也无法将目光移开。请观看下面的视频，亲自观看。

paras.en: "If you've ever been stung by a bee, you'll know it's a very painful process, but now we've been able to identify all the working parts packed into the tiny stinger," says entomologist Fiorella Ramirez-Esquivel of Macquarie University in Australia.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚麦考瑞大学昆虫学家 Fiorella Ramirez-Esquivel 表示：“如果你曾经被蜜蜂蛰过，你就会知道这是一个非常痛苦的过程，但现在我们已经能够识别出小毒刺中的所有工作部件。”

paras.en: "We've known since as early as 1910 that the venom sac of a honeybee stinger empties into a chamber with little pumping elements called valves, but until now we didn't know exactly how they work."
paras.zh: “我们早在 1910 年就知道蜜蜂毒刺的毒囊会排空到一个带有称为阀门的小泵元件的室中，但直到现在我们还不知道它们到底是如何工作的。”

paras.en: High-speed cameras captured the semi-translucent stinger as it plunges into a clear gel designed to mimic human skin, revealing the inner workings of this remarkable piece of biological machinery.
paras.zh: 高速摄像机捕捉到了半透明的毒刺插入模仿人类皮肤的透明凝胶中的情况，揭示了这一非凡生物机器的内部运作方式。

paras.en: "Despite sustained interest in the hymenopteran stinger, to date no direct observations of the venom pumping exist and our understanding of the biomechanics of venom delivery remains limited," the team writes.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“尽管人们对膜翅目毒刺一直感兴趣，但迄今为止，还没有对毒液泵送的直接观察，而且我们对毒液输送的生物力学的理解仍然有限。”

paras.en: "The stinger of the honey bee has unique properties including being reasonably large, translucent, and being able to autotomize [disconnect from the bee's body] during stinging."
paras.zh: “蜜蜂的毒刺具有独特的特性，包括相当大、半透明，并且能够在刺痛过程中自动切断[与蜜蜂身体的连接]。”

paras.en: It's surprising nobody has done this already, because there's some really wild stuff going on inside.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是还没有人这样做过，因为里面发生了一些非常疯狂的事情。

paras.en: Ramirez-Esquivel and team describe the stinger mechanism as a "unique double-piston micro-pump."
paras.zh: Ramirez-Esquivel 和团队将毒刺机构描述为“独特的双活塞微型泵”。

paras.en: They used forceps to guide the stinger into place, but then a pair of sharp barbs called lancets take over, with alternating jabs that drive the barb further into the 'skin' while also pumping venom.
paras.zh: 他们用镊子将毒刺引导到位，但随后一对被称为刺血针的锋利倒刺接管，交替刺击将倒刺进一步推入“皮肤”，同时也泵出毒液。

paras.en: Each lancet is attached to a corresponding valve inside the bulb chamber – that's the thicker part at the base of the stinger. These flexible valves alternately inflate to drive their attached lancet down, and deflate to retract it, squeezing past each other as they alternate.
paras.zh: 每个刺血针都连接到球室内相应的阀门上——这是刺针底部较厚的部分。这些柔性阀门交替充气以驱动其连接的刺血针向下，并放气以将其缩回，在交替时相互挤压。

paras.en: This also creates a downward pumping pressure on the connected venom chamber, drawing the liquid down towards the 'skin'.
paras.zh: 这也会在连接的毒液室上产生向下的泵压，将液体向下吸向“皮肤”。

paras.en: "Finally, and perhaps most dramatically, as the valves meet in the middle of the stroke, they change shape again to push past each other," says Ramirez-Esquivel.
paras.zh: “最后，也许是最戏剧性的，当阀门在冲程中间相遇时，它们再次改变形状以相互推挤，”拉米雷斯-埃斯基维尔说。

paras.en: "This is a remarkable strategy to pump fluid since maintaining a seal is vital to effectively transmit pressure. The unique geometry of the valves is the key; they act as collapsible pistons and – by pumping in opposite directions – they're able to deliver a continuous flow of venom."
paras.zh: “这是一种出色的泵送流体策略，因为保持密封对于有效传输压力至关重要。阀门的独特几何形状是关键；它们充当可折叠活塞，并且通过沿相反方向泵送，能够输送连续的毒液流。”

paras.en: As far as we know, this autonomous pumping 'design' is unique to worker honey bees. It's never been seen before; other members of the order Hymenoptera achieve their stings with wave-like contractions around the venom tract, a bit like how our gut pumps food through our body.
paras.zh: 据我们所知，这种自主泵送“设计”是工蜂所独有的。这是以前从未见过的；膜翅目的其他成员通过毒液道周围的波状收缩来实现叮咬，有点像我们的肠道将食物泵入体内的方式。

paras.en: The honeybee sting, on the other hand, is more similar to many human-made devices, like the syringes we use to inject drugs. Even these have only one relatively rigid piston in the chamber, which means they can't refill without creating backflow. Perhaps the bee stinger could inspire a device that can, for medical or research purposes.
paras.zh: 另一方面，蜜蜂蜇伤更类似于许多人造装置，例如我们用来注射毒品的注射器。即使这些在腔室中只有一个相对刚性的活塞，这意味着它们无法在不产生回流的情况下重新填充。也许蜂刺可以激发一种用于医疗或研究目的的设备。

paras.en: "The double piston design adds complexity but it's the key to the stinger being able to deliver venom continuously in a compact, autonomous unit," says Ramirez-Esquivel.
paras.zh: “双活塞设计增加了复杂性，但它是毒刺能够在紧凑的自主单元中连续输送毒液的关键，”拉米雷斯-埃斯基维尔说。

paras.en: The research has been published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

articles.title: Partial Vision Restored in Some Blind Patients With New Experimental Treatment
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Night vision often fades first, followed by a narrowing of peripheral vision. In retinitis pigmentosa, this progressive loss can eventually lead to blindness.
paras.zh: 夜视通常首先减弱，然后周边视力变窄。在色素性视网膜炎中，这种进行性丧失最终会导致失明。

paras.en: An experimental treatment has now helped some patients recover limited visual abilities.
paras.zh: 一项实验性治疗现已帮助一些患者恢复有限的视觉能力。

paras.en: The approach combines a gene injection with special goggles. In a small trial involving 10 people with profound vision loss in both eyes, some participants became better able to detect objects, locate them, and reach toward them while using the device.
paras.zh: 该方法将基因注射与特殊的护目镜结合起来。在一项涉及 10 名双眼严重视力丧失的人的小型试验中，一些参与者在使用该设备时能够更好地检测物体、定位物体并接近物体。

paras.en: The study in The New England Journal of Medicine was coauthored by ophthalmologist José-Alain Sahel at the University of Pittsburgh and vision researcher Botond Roska at the Institute of Molecular and Clinical Ophthalmology Basel in Switzerland.
paras.zh: 《新英格兰医学杂志》上的这项研究由匹兹堡大学眼科医生 José-Alain Sahel 和瑞士巴塞尔分子与临床眼科研究所视觉研究员 Botond Roska 共同撰写。

paras.en: Retinitis pigmentosa is a group of inherited disorders in which genetic changes damage the retina's photoreceptors, the cells that normally detect light.
paras.zh: 色素性视网膜炎是一组遗传性疾病，其中基因变化会损害视网膜的感光细胞（通常检测光的细胞）。

paras.en: Symptoms can begin in childhood or later, and progression varies. People without known affected relatives can also develop the disease.
paras.zh: 症状可能在儿童时期或更晚开始，并且进展情况各不相同。没有已知受影响亲属的人也可能患上这种疾病。

paras.en: Variants in more than 100 genes can cause it, complicating efforts to develop treatments for each genetic cause. This approach, called optogenetic therapy, gives nerve cells that survive the disease a new way to respond to light.
paras.zh: 超过 100 个基因的变异可能导致这种疾病，这使得针对每种遗传原因开发治疗方法的工作变得更加复杂。这种方法称为光遗传学疗法，为在疾病中存活的神经细胞提供了一种对光做出反应的新方法。

paras.en: Each participant received one injection into their worse-seeing eye. A modified virus delivered instructions for producing a light-sensitive protein called ChrimsonR into retinal ganglion cells, the nerve cells that transmit visual signals toward the brain.
paras.zh: 每位参与者的视力较差的眼睛都接受了一次注射。一种经过改造的病毒向视网膜神经节细胞（向大脑传输视觉信号的神经细胞）传递产生一种名为 ChrimsonR 的光敏蛋白的指令。

paras.en: "The gene therapy delivers a light sensor to the blind retina, making it light-sensitive again. The goggles provide light stimulation at the wavelength to which this sensor responds," Sahel and Roska told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “基因疗法将光传感器传送到盲人视网膜，使其再次对光敏感。护目镜以该传感器响应的波长提供光刺激，”萨赫勒和罗斯卡告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: A camera in the goggles captures changes in brightness. A processor turns those changes into patterns of amber light, which a projector directs onto the retina to activate the protein.
paras.zh: 护目镜中的摄像头捕捉亮度的变化。处理器将这些变化转化为琥珀色光的图案，投影仪将其投射到视网膜上以激活蛋白质。

paras.en: "In addition, the goggles adapt to outside light conditions and modify the signal to ensure optimal stimulation of the retina," Sahel and Roska said.
paras.zh: “此外，护目镜会适应外部光线条件并修改信号，以确保对视网膜的最佳刺激，”萨赫勒和罗斯卡说。

paras.en: Participants practiced using the goggles. During visual tests, their untreated eye was covered.
paras.zh: 参与者练习使用护目镜。在视力测试期间，他们未经治疗的眼睛被遮盖。

paras.en: The trial primarily assessed safety, but researchers also examined light sensitivity and object detection.
paras.zh: 该试验主要评估安全性，但研究人员还检查了光敏感性和物体检测。

paras.en: They measured the dimmest light participants could detect through the goggles before and after treatment. Seven showed increased sensitivity, ranging from about twofold to 62-fold. Six reached roughly a fourfold increase or more, which the team considered clinically meaningful.
paras.zh: 他们测量了治疗前后参与者通过护目镜所能检测到的最暗光线。其中 7 种表现出更高的灵敏度，范围从大约两倍到 62 倍。其中六人的数量增加了大约四倍或更多，该团队认为这具有临床意义。

paras.en: That threshold came from earlier research and was not specified beforehand in the trial protocol.
paras.zh: 该阈值来自早期研究，试验方案中并未事先指定。

paras.en: Eight participants completed object tests with and without the goggles. They tried to detect, locate, and touch a notebook or small box of staples, and distinguish the orientation of a bar.
paras.zh: 八名参与者在佩戴或不佩戴护目镜的情况下完成了物体测试。他们试图检测、定位和触摸笔记本或小订书钉盒，并区分条形的方向。

paras.en: Four consistently performed better at detecting the notebook with the goggles over repeated sessions spanning roughly a year to a year and a half. Others showed no consistent improvement across the tests.
paras.zh: 在大约一年到一年半的重复训练中，四人在使用护目镜检测笔记本电脑方面始终表现得更好。其他人在测试中没有表现出一致的改善。

paras.en: The criteria for classifying participants as responders were not specified beforehand.
paras.zh: 事先没有指定将参与者分类为响应者的标准。

paras.en: "Differences between patients in the increase in sensitivity may reflect how well the gene therapy vector reaches the retinal cells, or how many retinal cells remain, or other variables such as training to wear the goggles," Sahel and Roska explained.
paras.zh: 萨赫勒和罗斯卡解释说：“患者之间敏感性增加的差异可能反映了基因治疗载体到达视网膜细胞的程度，或者还有多少视网膜细胞，或者其他变量，例如佩戴护目镜的训练。”

paras.en: Better performance was associated with more training sessions, but the range of possible values included no association at all.
paras.zh: 更好的表现与更多的训练课程相关，但可能值的范围根本不包括任何关联。

paras.en: Brain recordings from five selected participants supported the possibility that visual signals reached the brain. Four had already responded in behavioral tests. For some estimates, the confidence interval included zero.
paras.zh: 五名选定参与者的大脑记录支持了视觉信号到达大脑的可能性。其中四人已经在行为测试中做出了反应。对于某些估计，置信区间包括零。

paras.en: "Safety was very good and is not a limitation," Sahel and Roska said. The authors cautioned that the safety findings came from 10 participants.
paras.zh: “安全性非常好，不是限制，”萨赫勒和罗斯卡说。作者警告说，安全性研究结果来自 10 名参与者。

paras.en: Researchers recorded 34 eye-related adverse events among nine participants, mostly mild or moderate. Seven developed inflammation inside the eye, which resolved with treatment without lasting consequences. One severe event involved a temporary blockage of the central retinal artery immediately after injection; it resolved within minutes after medication.
paras.zh: 研究人员记录了 9 名参与者的 34 起与眼睛相关的不良事件，大部分为轻度或中度。七人出现眼内炎症，经治疗后消退，没有造成持久后果。一项严重事件涉及注射后立即暂时阻塞视网膜中央动脉；用药后几分钟内就解决了。

paras.en: There were also 70 systemic adverse events, including six severe events. The principal investigator, with oversight from a data and safety monitoring board, judged none of the systemic events to be related to the gene therapy or injection. Three mild systemic events were linked to the goggles.
paras.zh: 还有 70 起全身不良事件，其中 6 起严重事件。主要研究者在数据和安全监测委员会的监督下，判断没有任何系统事件与基因治疗或注射有关。三起轻微的全身事件与护目镜有关。

paras.en: Four participants completed five years of follow-up. Several others were monitored for two to four and a half years, while two withdrew earlier.
paras.zh: 四名参与者完成了五年的随访。其他几人被监控了两到四年半，还有两人提前退出。

paras.en: The report expands on a 2021 study of one participant, whose results are included in the current group.
paras.zh: 该报告扩展了 2021 年对一名参与者进行的一项研究，其结果包含在当前组中。

paras.en: GenSight Biologics funded the trial, helped design it, and managed the data. The trial was not randomized and had no control arm. Further research is needed to assess its benefits and risks.
paras.zh: GenSight Biologics 资助了该试验，帮助设计并管理数据。该试验不是随机的，也没有对照组。需要进一步研究来评估其益处和风险。

paras.en: "What is still missing is the ability to recognize faces and to read; greater sensitivity of the optogenetic sensor would also be valuable," Sahel and Roska said.
paras.zh: “仍然缺少的是识别面孔和阅读的能力；光遗传学传感器更高的灵敏度也很有价值，”萨赫勒和罗斯卡说。

paras.en: "We are working to address these limitations."
paras.zh: “我们正在努力解决这些限制。”

paras.en: The research has been published in The New England Journal of Medicine.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《新英格兰医学杂志》上。

articles.title: Ovaries Develop an Intriguing Second Role After Menopause
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: Menopause has long been thought of as a terminal moment for the female reproductive system, when ovaries stop releasing eggs and presumably call it a day.
paras.zh: 长期以来，更年期一直被认为是女性生殖系统的终结时刻，此时卵巢停止释放卵子，大概就到此为止了。

paras.en: But this simplified image of ovarian retirement simply isn't holding up, as researchers look closer at what happens to these organs after menopause.
paras.zh: 但这种卵巢退休的简化形象根本站不住脚，因为研究人员更仔细地观察绝经后这些器官会发生什么。

paras.en: "In the ovary, we reach a point of no return with respect to fertility in which it's no longer producing eggs, and I would venture to say most people assume those ovaries are just sitting there doing nothing, similar to the appendix," says reproductive biologist Francesca Duncan of Northwestern University.
paras.zh: 西北大学的生殖生物学家弗朗西斯卡·邓肯（Francesca Duncan）说：“在卵巢中，我们的生育能力达到了一个不可逆转的地步，它不再产生卵子，我敢说大多数人都认为这些卵巢只是坐在那里什么也不做，就像阑尾一样。”

paras.en: "The ovary is not just a reproductive organ," says proteomics expert Birgit Schilling of the Buck Institute.

"It really influences how somebody ages because it speaks to all these other organs, such as the brain, and also to the bone, and women after menopause experience often a lot of bone problems. So, we think there is a connection between all these organs."
Schilling and Duncan led a new study published today in the scientific journal Aging Cell.
paras.zh: 席林和邓肯领导的一项新研究今天发表在科学杂志《衰老细胞》上。

paras.en: Their results suggest that for the ovary, menopause is much more like a career change than retirement.
paras.zh: 他们的结果表明，对于卵巢来说，更年期更像是职业转变，而不是退休。

paras.en: The researchers used mass spectrometry to look at which proteins were active in the healthy ovaries of 28 postmenopausal women, according to the tissue donor's age: 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and 70 and older.
These women had their ovaries surgically removed for various reasons, but none of the ovaries included in the study showed signs of disease.
paras.zh: 这些女性因各种原因接受了卵巢切除手术，但研究中的卵巢均未显示出疾病迹象。

paras.en: The results mirrored what Duncan found in the ovaries of mice in a study published earlier this year: the protein profiles produced by ovarian tissue shift progressively with age. In the human ovaries, a core set of seventeen proteins really characterized that shift.
paras.zh: 结果反映了邓肯在今年早些时候发表的一项研究中在小鼠卵巢中发现的情况：卵巢组织产生的蛋白质谱随着年龄的增长而逐渐变化。在人类卵巢中，由十七种蛋白质组成的核心组确实表征了这种转变。

paras.en: Ovaries from the 50-59 age group had more proteins related to regulating RNA and DNA, and maintaining the tissue structure and cells. In contrast, ovaries from the 70+ group had more proteins involved in lipid metabolism, innate immunity, and inflammation.
paras.zh: 50-59岁年龄段的卵巢含有更多与调节RNA和DNA、维持组织结构和细胞相关的蛋白质。相比之下，70岁以上组的卵巢含有更多参与脂质代谢、先天免疫和炎症的蛋白质。

paras.en: If ovaries were 'inert' after their reproductive years, that wouldn't be the case.
paras.zh: 如果卵巢在生育年龄后保持“惰性”，情况就不是这样了。

paras.en: "I was predicting that if we took a 50-year-old ovary, a 60-year-old ovary, a 70-year-old, an 80-year-old ovary, they would all look exactly the same, have no eggs, and basically be non-functional," Duncan says.
paras.zh: “我预测，如果我们取一个 50 岁的卵巢、一个 60 岁的卵巢、一个 70 岁的卵巢、一个 80 岁的卵巢，它们看起来都会完全一样，没有卵子，而且基本上没有功能，”邓肯说。

paras.en: "The fact that across species we're seeing this gives us confidence that this isn't just some random event, but something truly meaningful is happening in the biology."
paras.zh: “我们在不同物种中看到的这一事实让我们相信，这不仅仅是一些随机事件，而是生物学中正在发生的一些真正有意义的事情。”

paras.en: Life expectancies are generally stretching further than ever before, which means there's now far more postmenopausal people wandering around, whose bodies we still don't fully understand.
paras.zh: 预期寿命普遍比以往任何时候都延长，这意味着现在有更多的绝经后人四处游荡，但我们仍然无法完全了解他们的身体。

paras.en: Ovarian cancer risk is much higher after menopause, and the new study reveals why this might be the case.
paras.zh: 绝经后卵巢癌的风险要高得多，这项新研究揭示了为什么会出现这种情况。

paras.en: Age-related changes in ovarian tissue and immune cells at the protein level create an environment ideal for tumors by loading the extracellular matrix with collagen.
paras.zh: 卵巢组织和免疫细胞在蛋白质水平上发生与年龄相关的变化，通过在细胞外基质中装载胶原蛋白，为肿瘤创造了理想的环境。

paras.en: The ovarian tissue samples in this study were, of course, tumor-free, but proteins previously linked to ovarian cancer were abundant, most prominently in the ovaries of women in their 60s.
paras.zh: 当然，这项研究中的卵巢组织样本是无肿瘤的，但之前与卵巢癌相关的蛋白质却很丰富，尤其是在 60 多岁女性的卵巢中。

paras.en: "It's not that all postmenopausal women get ovarian cancer, but we know that that fibrotic inflammatory environment is certainly an environment that cancer cells prefer to home in on," Duncan says.
paras.zh: 邓肯说：“并不是所有绝经后妇女都会患卵巢癌，但我们知道纤维化炎症环境肯定是癌细胞更喜欢栖息的环境。”

paras.en: "This is all consistent with the idea that the aging ovary is a potential third hit for ovarian cancer, with the first hit being genetic and the second hit being environmental. So can we target the aging ovary therapeutically to lower the risk of ovarian cancer, or can we develop novel biomarkers of ovarian cancer?"
paras.zh: “这与衰老的卵巢是卵巢癌潜在的第三次打击的观点是一致的，第一次打击是遗传性的，第二次打击是环境性的。那么我们是否可以通过治疗来针对衰老的卵巢来降低卵巢癌的风险，或者我们可以开发新的卵巢癌生物标志物吗？”

paras.en: With an initial 'roadmap' of ovarian aging now established, researchers can begin to probe these more nuanced questions.
paras.zh: 随着卵巢衰老的初步“路线图”的建立，研究人员可以开始探讨这些更微妙的问题。

paras.en: These findings could have important implications for healthcare in people's post-reproductive years, and among people who have their ovaries removed.
paras.zh: 这些发现可能对生育后期以及卵巢切除患者的医疗保健产生重要影响。

paras.en: The research has been published in Aging Cell.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《衰老细胞》杂志上。

articles.title: The secret to handling stress better may start at breakfast

paras.en: The secret to handling stress better may start at breakfast
Eating breakfast, exercising, and sleeping well could help build a more flexible, resilient mind that handles stress better.

- Your daily routine could have a bigger impact on your ability to handle stress than you realize. A Binghamton University study of approximately 400 college students found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological flexibility, which helps people adapt to stressful situations. Poor sleep and unhealthy eating habits, meanwhile, were linked to lower flexibility and resilience.

Feeling overwhelmed by stress or struggling to adjust when things go wrong? Everyday habits such as eating a nutritious breakfast, getting regular exercise, and sleeping enough may play an important role in how well your mind handles difficult situations.

New research from Binghamton University suggests that these healthy routines are connected to a mental skill called psychological flexibility, which helps people adapt to challenges and recover from stressful experiences.

Psychological flexibility refers to the ability to adjust your thoughts, emotions, and actions as circumstances change. Rather than becoming trapped in negative thinking or overwhelmed by frustration, people with greater psychological flexibility can recognize their emotions, consider their options, and respond in a more productive way.

"You might know someone who stays cool under pressure," said Lina Begdache, an associate professor of health and wellness studies at Binghamton University and lead author of the research. "The kind of person who misses a flight and, instead of panicking, calmly adapts to the situation. This person may still feel stressed, but they're better able to manage it through psychological flexibility."

"People may say that these are resilient people, but they also have what's called psychological flexibility. They're able to change the way they think about the situation and then use brain resources to handle the stress."
How Breakfast, Sleep, and Exercise Relate to Mental Resilience

To explore the relationship between lifestyle choices and emotional resilience, Begdache worked with Jason Cherry, a former Binghamton assistant professor of physical therapy, and former student Alexander J. Talkachov.
The researchers collected anonymous survey responses from approximately 400 college students, gathering information about their diets, sleep patterns, exercise habits, and other lifestyle factors.

Their findings revealed an important connection between healthy routines and the ability to cope with stress. Students who reported healthier habits, including regular physical activity and consistent breakfast consumption, also tended to demonstrate greater psychological flexibility and resilience.
The study identified several notable associations:
- Regular breakfast consumption: Eating breakfast at least five times per week was associated with greater resilience, with psychological flexibility helping explain the relationship.
- Adequate sleep: Students who slept fewer than six hours generally reported lower levels of both resilience and psychological flexibility.
- Physical activity: Exercise lasting 20 minutes or longer was associated with greater psychological flexibility and an improved ability to cope with stress.
- Fish oil intake: Taking fish oil several times per week was linked to better psychological flexibility.

The opposite pattern also emerged. Students who reported less healthy behaviors, including frequent fast food consumption and insufficient sleep, tended to show greater psychological rigidity, meaning they had more difficulty adjusting their thoughts and behaviors when circumstances changed.
Because the research relied on survey responses, the results demonstrate associations rather than proving that these habits directly improve psychological flexibility or resilience.
Why Psychological Flexibility Matters for Stress

According to Begdache, psychological flexibility gives people the mental space to recognize what they are experiencing instead of becoming completely absorbed by their stress. This ability to reassess a situation can make it easier to understand difficult emotions and determine how to respond.
paras.zh: 贝格达什认为，心理灵活性为人们提供了心理空间来认识他们正在经历的事情，而不是完全被压力所吸引。这种重新评估情况的能力可以使人更容易理解困难的情绪并确定如何应对。

paras.en: She explained that improvements in diet and lifestyle may help support this kind of mental adaptability.
paras.zh: 她解释说，饮食和生活方式的改善可能有助于支持这种心理适应能力。

paras.en: "When we're under stress, we feel like we fuse with the stress. We live the stress. But psychological flexibility is like stepping back and thinking, 'I feel this because of that. What can I do?' Identifying your emotions sometimes helps you find the solution for these emotions," said Begdache.
paras.zh: “当我们承受压力时，我们感觉自己与压力融为一体。我们生活在压力中。但心理灵活性就像退后一步思考，‘我因为那个而有这个感觉。我能做什么？’识别你的情绪有时可以帮助你找到这些情绪的解决方案，”贝格达什说。

paras.en: The findings also build on Begdache's previous research, which linked nutritious diets to greater resilience and poorer dietary habits to reduced resilience.

The latest study offers a possible explanation for that relationship. Rather than influencing resilience alone, diet and lifestyle may support psychological flexibility, which in turn helps people manage stress more effectively.
paras.zh: 最新的研究为这种关系提供了可能的解释。饮食和生活方式不仅可以影响复原力，还可以支持心理灵活性，从而帮助人们更有效地管理压力。

paras.en: "The new finding here is that diet and lifestyle don't just make you resilient by themselves. They help you build the psychological flexibility, which, in turn, makes you a resilient person."
The study, "Dietary and lifestyle factors and resilience: the role of psychological flexibility as a mediator," was published in the Journal of American College Health.
paras.zh: 这项研究题为“饮食和生活方式因素与复原力：心理灵活性作为中介的作用”，发表在《美国大学健康杂志》上。
